workflow_name: Clang-tidy static analysis (Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12, Clang-18, Clang-tidy-18)
author: byungilm
title: ARM64 CMake configure fails because sccache times out waiting for server startup
signature: sccache error timed out waiting for server startup maybe the remote service is unreachable cmake test c compiler check for working c compiler broken|External Service

failed_jobs.name: Build-aarch64 / Build
failed_jobs.symptom: CMake configure step fails during the 'Check for working C compiler' test: sccache cannot be launched to wrap /usr/bin/cc, so the C compiler smoke test fails and CMake aborts configuration.

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_clang_tidy
failed_jobs.symptom: Downstream status-aggregation job fails because the upstream Build-aarch64 job failed.

key_errors: CMake Error at /usr/local/share/cmake-3.26/Modules/CMakeTestCCompiler.cmake:67 (message): The C compiler "/usr/bin/cc" is not able to compile a simple test program.
sccache: error: Timed out waiting for server startup. Maybe the remote service is unreachable?
-- Check for working C compiler: /usr/bin/cc - broken
root_cause: CMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER/CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER are set to sccache with SCCACHE_AZURE_CONNECTION_STRING pointing at the Azure Blob remote cache. During CMake's compiler-identification try-compile step, the sccache client process could not start/connect its local coordinating server within its startup timeout (the error explicitly points at the remote Azure service being unreachable), causing the trivial test-compile invocation to fail and CMake to mark the C compiler as broken before any real GPU plugin source was touched. This is unrelated to the PR's actual change (a one-line null-cast guard in src/plugins/intel_gpu/src/plugin/transformations_pipeline.cpp); the automatic retry (run_attempt 2) proceeded past CMake configure successfully, confirming the failure was a transient sccache/Azure connectivity hiccup rather than a code defect.
reproduction_steps: N/A - not reproducible outside CI; requires the CI runner's sccache client/Azure Blob remote-cache connectivity. Locally, a build without CMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=sccache (or with SCCACHE disabled) configures and builds normally.
recommended_actions: No code change needed for PR #39524; the failure is infrastructure-related, not caused by the PR diff.
Re-run the failed Build-aarch64 job (already succeeded on run_attempt 2).

If this sccache startup timeout recurs frequently, consider raising SCCACHE_STARTUP_TIMEOUT or adding a short retry/backoff around the sccache server bootstrap in the build job, and monitor Azure Blob storage availability for the SCCACHE_AZURE_* backend.
prevention_strategies: Add a lightweight pre-flight check in the build composite action that verifies sccache can start and reach the configured remote storage before invoking CMake, failing fast with a clearer diagnostic, or falling back to local-only caching (SCCACHE_IGNORE_SERVER_IO_ERROR is already set to 1, but the client never reaches the point where that matters if server startup itself times out). Track Azure Blob Storage health/latency for the sccache backend to catch recurring outages early.
historical_context: No prior CI Doctor MQ pattern records this exact sccache 'Timed out waiting for server startup' signature; this is the first occurrence tracked. A related but distinct ARM64 cross-compilation PCH failure (signature_hash 5b4b1e6917a69856, category Infrastructure) has recurred multiple times since 2026-09-24 but is a different root cause (stale cmake_pch.hxx.gch reuse across differently-configured re-builds, not sccache connectivity).
